Setting the scene

text.content: Meridian's agent is connected to three capabilities: a Document Store, an HTTP Node for live data, and an iteration flow for briefings. Each connection required custom configuration: credentials, URL endpoints, response handling, and error logic written specifically for each integration.

What MCP is

text.content: The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that defines a universal interface for how AI agents connect to external tools and data sources. It was introduced by Anthropic in late 2024 and has since been adopted across agent frameworks, development environments, and enterprise platforms.

rich_text.plain_text: The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that defines a universal interface for how AI agents connect to external tools and data sources. It was introduced by Anthropic in late 2024 and has since been adopted across agent frameworks, development environments, and enterprise platforms.

text.content: The analogy that captures it most clearly is USB-C. Before standardised ports, connecting a peripheral required knowing which specific connector each device used. USB-C provides a universal connection standard and any compatible peripheral connects to any compatible device through the same port. MCP does the same for AI agents and external tools.

text.content: How MCP works in Agentflow v2

rich_text.plain_text: How MCP works in Agentflow v2

text.content: Agentflow v2 allows MCP tools to be connected as part of the workflow, rather than functioning solely as agent tools. Custom MCPs can also be created independently, without depending on platform-provided integrations. MCP is widely considered an industry standard and is typically supported and maintained by the official providers.

Cross-framework interoperability:

text.content: An MCP server built to expose Meridian's Document Store can be consumed by a Flowise agent, a Langflow agent, and a Claude environment simultaneously without rebuilding the integration for each platform.

Reduced integration overhead:

text.content: Instead of writing custom connectors for every tool in every framework, a team builds one MCP server per tool. Any MCP-compatible agent can then access it through the same standardised interface.

Takeaway:

text.content: MCP does for AI agent integrations what USB-C did for hardware connectivity — it replaces a fragmented landscape of custom connectors with a single universal standard. One MCP server per tool. Any compatible agent can use it. When a new capability is added to the server, all connected agents discover it automatically. For Meridian's agent and its clients, this means integrations built once become available everywhere.
